lesson.title: End of the Cold War
lesson.summary: How Soviet economic weakness, Gorbachev's reforms, and the revolutions of 1989 ended the Cold War.
learningGoals: Explain the causes of the end of the Cold War.
lesson.bigIdea: Economic stagnation, costly commitments, and reforms that loosened control allowed Eastern Europeans to overthrow communism and the Soviet Union to dissolve.
lesson.context: By the 1980s, the Soviet economy could not keep pace with Western technology or consumer goods.

sections.title: Soviet decline and reform

blocks.text: In the 1970s, détente, a relaxation of tensions, produced arms control treaties, but it ended when the Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan in 1979. The war cost lives and money for a decade. Meanwhile, the Soviet economy stagnated, and falling oil prices in the 1980s cut its income.

US President Ronald Reagan increased military spending. Mikhail Gorbachev, the Soviet leader from 1985, introduced glasnost, or openness, which allowed more criticism, and perestroika, a restructuring of the economy. He also negotiated arms reductions with the United States.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Gorbachev's reforms were meant to save the Soviet system, but openness let people criticize it, and restructuring disrupted the economy.

sections.takeaway: Economic weakness and Gorbachev's reforms loosened the Soviet grip at home and abroad.

sections.title: 1989 and 1991

blocks.text: In Poland, the trade union Solidarity, led by Lech Wałęsa, won a semi-free election in 1989. Gorbachev refused to send troops, and the revolutions of 1989 spread across Eastern Europe. The Berlin Wall fell in November, and Germany reunited in 1990.
Nationalist movements inside the Soviet Union demanded independence. After a failed coup by hard-liners in August 1991, the Soviet Union dissolved in December into fifteen independent states.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: The Cold War did not end only because of US pressure. Soviet economic problems, Gorbachev's choices, and protests in Eastern Europe were all essential.

sections.takeaway: Popular revolutions and Soviet restraint ended communist rule in Eastern Europe.

connections.title: A globalizing world
connections.body: The end of the Cold War opened former communist states to world trade, a theme of Unit 9.
